section_summary: The section concludes a discussion of political cells in trade unions and recommends democratic elections, financial accountability, frequent meetings, and worker education as safeguards. A covering despatch then forwards a 1948 study of Japanese teachers’ unions. The study traces their prewar origins, postwar economic pressures, and the emergence of competing radical and conservative unions.

subfiles.title: Democratic Trade Union Principles
subfiles.about: Explains how political cells can capture unions and recommends democratic safeguards for Japanese trade unionists.
subfiles.summary: The pamphlet describes secret caucuses, meeting disruption, intimidation, and front organizations as methods of gaining control over unions. Drawing on American experience and principles proposed for Japanese unions, it urges frequent membership meetings, secret ballots, accountable officers, audited finances, and worker education.

subfiles.title: A History of Teachers’ Unions in Japan
subfiles.from: Education Research, Analysis and Research Division, Civil Information and Education Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.about: Studies the origins, programs, and early postwar development of Japan’s national teachers’ unions.
subfiles.summary: The introduction outlines the study’s scope, sources, and a chronology ending with the June 1947 union amalgamation. The chapters included here examine the prewar official education association, Occupation reforms, and inflation’s effect on teachers’ livelihoods. They then describe the competing programs and conflicts of the Zenkyo and Nikkyo, followed by the formation of the Seikyo.
